# Results — Study 701 (Crab-Harmonic)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
Scott Carney's **Crab** harmonic, marketed as the **sharpest, most exact** member of
the harmonic-pattern family: a five-point X-A-B-C-D structure where B retraces XA by
**0.382-0.618** (shallower than the Butterfly's fixed 0.786), C retraces AB somewhere
in **0.382-0.886**, and **D extends the ORIGINAL XA leg by exactly 1.618x, past point
X** — a single, tight target rather than the Butterfly's 1.27-1.618 *range*. Believers
expect a reversal the moment price touches D. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Basket: SPY, QQQ,
AAPL, MSFT, TSLA, NVDA — identical to siblings
[699-butterfly-harmonic](../../699-butterfly-harmonic/) and
[700-bat-harmonic](../../700-bat-harmonic/), for apples-to-apples comparison.*

## The protocol

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Pivot detection | percentage-threshold zigzag on daily closes, **pct = 2%**; a pivot is recorded only at its **confirmation bar** (never the earlier, still-unconfirmed extreme) |
| Crab arm — structural bands (both arms) | AB retraces XA by **0.382-0.618** (shallower than the Butterfly's fixed 0.786, close to the Bat's 0.382-0.50); BC retraces AB by **0.382-0.886** (the shared XABCD band) |
| Crab arm — defining ratio | **D = X − 1.618 × (A − X)**, i.e. D extends the *original* XA leg 1.618x **past** point X — the single sharpest, most extreme target in the harmonic zoo |
| Placebo arm | identical structural pivots (same AB/BC bands, same candidate pool), but each candidate's D-extension *target* is drawn uniformly from [0.85, 2.20], kept ≥ 0.15 clear of 1.618 — "any extension zone near X", not specifically Carney's 1.618 |
| D-touch scan | forward window of **120 sessions** from C's confirmation bar; first bar whose high-low range brackets D (or closes within 0.75% of it) |
| Execution | enter the fade at the touch bar's **own close** (the touch is observed intrabar via that bar's high-low range — one documented convention, identical in both arms) |
| Base-rate control | ``n`` random entry days per ticker, matched to the **same empirical bullish/bearish mix** as the real Crab touches, pooled over **20 seeds** — neutralizes the equity-drift confound a directional rule inherits on an upward-drifting tape |
| Bonferroni | pooled headline + 6 per-ticker splits (5-day) = **7 tests**; critical \|*t*\| raised from 2.0 to **2.69** (family-wise α = 0.05, normal approximation) |
| Costs | one round trip = **2 × one-way cost × NAV**; net figures at 5 / 10 bps one-way |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC) *t* of the mean return against 0 (events can cluster in time); Welch *t* for the base-rate and placebo arm-vs-arm comparisons; Wilson interval on hit rate |

No survivorship: six large, currently-listed single names/ETFs, individually named — not a
membership-conditioned panel.

## The headline — Crab XABCD, forward returns at D

Pooled confirmed pivots: **6,055** → Crab XABCD candidates: **226** → D-touches: **76**.

| horizon | n | hit rate | mean (bps/event) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 76 | 53.9% | −18.85  | −0.38 |
| **5-day (headline)** | **76** | **39.5%** | **−82.70** | **−1.30** |
| 10-day | 76 | 40.8% | −253.84 | **−2.40** |

Hit rate (5-day): **39.5%** (Wilson 95% [29.2%, 50.7%]) — below a coin flip. The
headline mean is *negative* at every horizon tested, and by 10 days the loss is large
enough to individually clear the naive |*t*| ≥ 2 bar — in the **losing** direction: the
mechanical Crab fade does not merely fail to find a reversal, it loses money on
average, increasingly so the longer it is held.

## Per-instrument (5-day, gross)

| Ticker | *n* | mean (bps) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 4  | +312.64 | n/a (n < 6) |
| QQQ  | 12 | +99.34  | +1.88 |
| AAPL | 11 | **−255.74** | **−2.45** |
| MSFT | 11 | +143.03 | +1.14 |
| TSLA | 16 | −57.46  | −0.28 |
| NVDA | 22 | **−298.59** | **−2.43** |

Two of six tickers (AAPL, NVDA) individually clear the uncorrected *t* ≥ 2 bar — both
in the **losing** direction. The two names carrying the pooled sample's negative tilt
(NVDA, AAPL) are also the two with the most candidates (22 and 11), so the pooled
result is not one noisy outlier; it is the modal outcome.

## Signal axis — Crab fade vs a random-day BASE RATE, Bonferroni-corrected

The base rate redraws, per ticker and pooled over 20 seeds, the same number of random
entry days with the same empirical bullish/bearish mix as the real Crab touches — the
equity-drift confound a directional rule inherits on an upward-drifting tape.

| horizon | Crab mean (bps) | base-rate mean (bps, n=1,520) | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | −18.85  | −1.44  | −0.36 |
| **5-day (headline)** | **−82.70** | −34.88 | **−0.61** |
| 10-day | −253.84 | −42.36 | −2.11 |

Per-ticker, 5-day, Crab vs its own matched-mix base rate:

| Ticker | Crab *n* | Crab mean (bps) | base-rate mean (bps) | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 4  | +312.64 | +20.38 | +1.60 |
| QQQ  | 12 | +99.34  | +12.33 | +0.94 |
| AAPL | 11 | −255.74 | −28.13 | **−2.05** |
| MSFT | 11 | +143.03 | −13.96 | +1.15 |
| TSLA | 16 | −57.46  | −82.13 | +0.10 |
| NVDA | 22 | −298.59 | −50.14 | −1.54 |

**Bonferroni correction across 7 tests** (pooled headline + 6 per-ticker splits, 5-day):
critical |*t*| = **2.69** (family-wise α = 0.05, normal approximation).

- **1 of 7 tests clears the uncorrected |*t*| ≥ 2 bar** (AAPL, Welch *t* = −2.05) — and
  it is a *loss* relative to the base rate, the opposite of what the claim predicts.
- **0 of 7 survive Bonferroni.** There is no honest reading of this basket in which
  fading the Crab's D beats a directionally-matched coin flip; if anything, the pooled
  point estimate (Welch *t* = −0.61) and the 10-day split (Welch *t* = −2.11, outside
  the formal 5-day test family but reported for completeness) both point the *wrong*
  way.

## Tradability axis — the fade timer, net of costs

One round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV per event.

| hold | gross mean (bps) | net @ 5 bps (bps) | net @ 10 bps (bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | −18.85 (t=−0.38)  | −28.85 (t=−0.58)  | −38.85 (t=−0.78)  |
| 3-day  | −83.17 (t=−1.27)  | −93.17 (t=−1.42)  | −103.17 (t=−1.57) |
| **5-day** | **−82.70 (t=−1.30)** | **−92.70 (t=−1.46)** | **−102.70 (t=−1.61)** |
| 10-day | −253.84 (t=−2.40) | −263.84 (t=−2.50) | −273.84 (t=−2.59) |
| 20-day | −503.01 (t=−2.76) | −513.01 (t=−2.81) | −523.01 (t=−2.87) |

Every single hold length is negative on average, gross and net, and costs only make it
worse. By 20 days the fade loses **503 bps gross on average** — a statistically
significant *loss* (*t* = −2.76). There is no horizon at which the Crab's D-touch fade
is both profitable and certified; the honest reading is that the tape tends to
*continue*, not reverse, past the Crab's 1.618 extension.

## Third axis (myth-check) — does the precise 1.618 extension beat a placebo extension zone?

Identical pivots and structural AB/BC bands; only the D-extension *target* differs
(Crab: fixed 1.618; placebo: drawn per-candidate from [0.85, 2.20], excluding a ±0.15
band around 1.618).

| horizon | Crab mean (bps) | placebo mean (bps) | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | −18.85  | −56.29  | +0.57 |
| **5-day (headline)** | **−82.70** | −115.68 | **+0.28** |
| 10-day | −253.84 | −347.94 | +0.59 |

Placebo candidates: 226 → placebo D-touches: 79.

Per-instrument, 5-day, Crab vs placebo:

| Ticker | Crab mean (bps) | placebo mean (bps) | beats placebo? |
|---|--:|--:|:--:|
| SPY  | +312.64 | −80.99  | **yes** |
| QQQ  | +99.34  | +134.71 | no |
| AAPL | −255.74 | −91.02  | no |
| MSFT | +143.03 | −6.68   | **yes** |
| TSLA | −57.46  | −335.39 | **yes** |
| NVDA | −298.59 | −147.58 | no |

Crab beats the placebo on **3 of 6** tickers — a coin flip — and at the pooled headline
horizon the Welch *t* is a negligible +0.28. Carney's specific, "sharpest" 1.618
extension shows no detectable edge over an arbitrary nearby extension zone built from
the identical pivot geometry; both arms lose money on average, so "beating the
placebo" here mostly means "losing slightly less."

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic mean-reverting price index (tunable `mean_rev` knob toward a slow EMA),
pooled across a **synthetic 6-name basket per seed** (mirrors the real pooled sample
size); no network.

| world | *n* (pooled) | mean (bps/event) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (`mean_rev = 0`), **20 seeds** | ~8/seed | — | mean **−0.13** (sd 1.10), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted `mean_rev = 0.12` (seed 701) | 8 | +394.01 | **+4.64** |

The null fires at close to the nominal ~5% false-positive rate expected of a *t* ≥ 2
threshold over 20 independent draws, and a planted mean-reversion tendency lights up
sharply. The pipeline can find a real Crab-shaped reversal effect when one is actually
there — the negative real-tape result above is the genuine article, not a broken
detector.  *(A faithful-engine / power check only; never cited in support of the
real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The Crab's 5-day fade-at-D return is **−82.70 bps/event, HAC
  *t* = −1.30** — negative and not even individually significant, with a hit rate
  (39.5%) *below* a coin flip. Against the drift-matched base rate the pooled Welch
  *t* is −0.61 (Crab **underperforms** a directionally-matched random entry), and
  **0 of 7 Bonferroni-corrected tests** (pooled + 6 per-ticker, critical |*t*| = 2.69)
  survive. At 10 days the pooled fade turns individually significant in the *losing*
  direction (HAC *t* = −2.40) — if anything the tape tends to continue past D, not
  reverse there.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Every hold length (1/3/5/10/20 days) is negative on
  average, gross and net; costs only compound the loss; by 20 days the fade loses
  **503 bps gross** on average, a statistically significant loss (*t* = −2.76). There
  is no horizon at which this trade is both profitable and certified.
- **"Beats a placebo extension zone (i.e. is 1.618 the 'sharpest, most exact' ratio, as
  Carney claims)?" — BUSTED.** The Crab arm beats its own placebo control on only 3 of
  6 tickers (a coin flip), and the pooled 5-day Welch *t* (+0.28) shows no detectable
  specificity for 1.618 over an arbitrary nearby extension built from the identical
  pivots — consistent with siblings
  [699-butterfly-harmonic](../699-butterfly-harmonic/) and
  [700-bat-harmonic](../700-bat-harmonic/)'s finding that Fibonacci ratio labels add
  nothing over a randomized control on the same six tapes.
